final_answer:
I found and fixed the client-side cause: the private key had mode `0644`, so SSH ignored it. I changed it to `0600`; the key’s contents were unchanged.

I couldn’t verify either connection yet. The initial failed attempts triggered SSH’s temporary rate-limit penalty on `server1`, which is on the jump path for both hosts. Retries were still being rejected with “Not allowed at this time” / connection reset, so access to `server2` and `server4` remains unverified. Once that penalty clears, retry both connections.
